cells.tense: You are here, at the end that is finally happening, and it is going through.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: With the person nearest what's ending, keep giving what's yours and taking what's offered — both directions, no tally at the close.
cells.core:
The closeness you're in runs both directions, and it's carrying an ending with it. Something is finishing out in the open. You aren't dragging it past the place it already ended, and you aren't going numb to dodge the goodbye. That is why the people near you can stay near you while it happens — nobody is being asked to hold a door shut.

What you have already is proportion by feel: you give what's yours, you take what's offered, nothing counted. The growth part is to keep that moving out loud — tell one person what is ending and what you need after. Then trust the exchange to keep flowing without a record of it. The feeling moves through instead of pooling.
cells.sheetLine: What's ending is finishing cleanly, and you're still here for it.
cells.verb: Letting what is finished finish so what is next can begin
cells.place: In closeness where two people feel the same thing and keep their own sides

cells.tense: You will keep ending things before they've had a chance to end on their own.
cells.act: stay in contact while it is hard
cells.ask: A bond you were about to close this month — stay in contact across the next hard stretch, not fixing anything and not walking out. Let what's carried reach you; hold your own ground in it.
cells.core:
Endings are easy to feel coming, and lately they arrive early. Close it first, before it can go somewhere outside your control — the ending feels like freedom, but the clearing is outrunning what actually needed to end. Anyone watching can tell the exit is being rehearsed.

You don't have to read the outcome. Stay in contact while it's hard — one bond you were ready to sever, one difficult stretch, this month. Sit in it without fixing anything and without leaving. Let what the other person carries reach you, and hold your own ground in it. If the end comes, let it come from what's real rather than from getting ahead of it.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is coming early because you're running it.
cells.verb: Letting what is finished finish so what is next can begin

cells.tense: You kept something alive past its end and called it loyalty.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Follow one pull you already feel toward something new — a place, a person, a first step — and give today's hours to that direction instead of the finished thing.
cells.core:
Someone or something is finished and you are still at its door. Your time, your worry, your staying keep going back there, and it's already gone. Loyalty is the name you've given it. The real thing is that no ending gets to happen near you at all, and your closeness sits constant while the thing it's attached to is past.

The way out isn't a feeling you're waiting on. Go where the pull already is — one direction you genuinely want, one step taken today, before you feel ready. Being done with the old thing first isn't the price; the step is what lets the door close. The desire you already carry does the work once your energy stops going backward.

cells.tense: Something is ending in you and you have not looked at it.
cells.act: build the smallest structure that holds it
cells.ask: Give what has finished in you the smallest shape that holds it — a time, a place, the next move, set down together. A container, not a verdict.
cells.core:
Something has stopped and you keep moving as if it hasn't. You don't know what it is — a role, a hope, the shape a closeness used to have — and not knowing keeps it open. There's no story about it you'd recognize, because you haven't given it one.

You can stop there. Build the smallest thing that holds it: set the ending down along with when and where you'll meet it, and the next move. Not a verdict on the bond, not a decision only you can make — a container. Once the ending has a shape you can carry it instead of it carrying you. What you couldn't see becomes something you've held once, and it starts to move.
